questions.stem: What does the default CLZ-300 configuration manage?

options.A: A public zone and registrar

optionExplanations.A: Neither is enabled by default.
optionExplanations.B: Zone creation defaults to false.
optionExplanations.C: This lesson models public DNS.
optionExplanations.D: That belongs to CLZ-330.

questions.stem: Which pair of inputs enables an owned public zone?

options.A: create_public_dns_zone=false and any name

optionExplanations.A: False leaves the zone absent.
optionExplanations.B: These do not enable the zone.
optionExplanations.C: The prefix is not domain ownership.
optionExplanations.D: Both intent and domain are required.

questions.stem: A learner has no domain. Which exercise remains appropriate?

options.A: Review the default no-zone plan

optionExplanations.A: It needs no registrar change.
optionExplanations.B: The learner lacks ownership.
optionExplanations.C: Delegation requires deliberate coordination.
optionExplanations.D: The reserved placeholder is unsuitable.

questions.stem: An owned zone exists in Azure but still resolves elsewhere. What is missing?

options.A: A VM inside the zone
options.C: Correct delegation at the domain registrar

optionExplanations.A: A zone is not a VM network.
optionExplanations.B: The resource-group region does not delegate DNS.
optionExplanations.C: Azure zone creation does not update it.
optionExplanations.D: DNS delegation does not use that secret.

questions.stem: Which output identifies the servers used for delegation?

options.A: resource_group_name

optionExplanations.A: This identifies the management container.
optionExplanations.B: This is the resource-group region.
optionExplanations.C: This exposes the zone's authoritative servers.
optionExplanations.D: Use the actual assigned servers.

questions.stem: Why is the default public_dns_name_servers value empty?

options.A: No public DNS zone was created

optionExplanations.A: The conditional output returns an empty list.
optionExplanations.B: An empty optional output is expected.
optionExplanations.C: The configuration does not manage registrars.
optionExplanations.D: The DNS service does not require one.

questions.stem: What does count=0 on azurerm_dns_zone.public mean?

options.A: Create a zone with zero records
options.C: Hide the zone from output only
options.D: No instances of that resource are planned

optionExplanations.A: Zero count removes the resource instance.
optionExplanations.B: Count is not a pricing setting.
optionExplanations.C: It affects the resource itself.
optionExplanations.D: Count controls resource instance creation.

questions.stem: Before applying an enabled zone, what should the learner inspect?

options.A: Only the terminal color scheme
options.B: The saved plan and exact owned zone name
options.C: Only the number of Terraform files

optionExplanations.A: It provides no change evidence.
optionExplanations.B: Review intended changes before applying.
optionExplanations.C: File count does not describe the plan.
optionExplanations.D: It does not verify this deployment.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly separates Azure DNS from a registrar?

options.A: Azure DNS hosts records; registration is separate
options.B: Azure DNS purchases every hosted domain
options.C: A registrar runs Terraform state locking
options.D: Creating a zone grants domain ownership

optionExplanations.A: Hosting does not purchase domain ownership.
optionExplanations.B: A zone is not a domain purchase.
optionExplanations.C: That is a backend function.
optionExplanations.D: Ownership remains with the registrant.

questions.stem: Two Azure zones share a domain name in different resource groups. What decides Internet authority?

options.A: The shortest resource-group name

optionExplanations.A: DNS does not rank resource-group names.
optionExplanations.B: Provider age does not control delegation.
optionExplanations.C: Creation alone does not select an authority.
optionExplanations.D: They have separately assigned servers.

questions.stem: Delegation was corrected, but some clients show old results. What should be considered?

options.A: VM disk caching mode

optionExplanations.A: It is unrelated to DNS caches.
optionExplanations.B: Old answers can persist until cache expiry.
optionExplanations.C: That does not flush recursive caches.
optionExplanations.D: That does not correct cached delegation.

questions.stem: What does the zone name represent in this optional lesson?

options.A: A URL including https and a path
options.D: The owned domain's DNS zone apex

optionExplanations.A: A DNS zone name is not a URL.
optionExplanations.B: Subscription selection is separate.
optionExplanations.C: DNS names are not credentials.
optionExplanations.D: Records are hosted beneath that zone.

questions.stem: Which change is outside this Terraform configuration?

options.A: Creating the lesson resource group

optionExplanations.A: The lesson explicitly manages it.
optionExplanations.B: The conditional resource manages it.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform destroy handles managed resources.
optionExplanations.D: Delegation is managed separately.

questions.stem: Before moving production delegation, which evidence is valuable?

options.A: Only a screenshot of Terraform's logo
options.B: The previous name servers and rollback procedure
options.D: A randomly chosen zone in another tenant

optionExplanations.A: It cannot restore DNS.
optionExplanations.B: Rollback must restore external authority.
optionExplanations.C: Deletion loses management information.
optionExplanations.D: It is not an approved rollback target.

questions.stem: After destroying this lab, what might still need a separate action?

options.A: Destroying CLZ-310's state account automatically
options.C: Restoring registrar delegation if it was changed

optionExplanations.A: That belongs to a separate lesson.
optionExplanations.B: Cleanup must remain within ownership.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform does not own that external setting.
optionExplanations.D: Learners do not own the service.

questions.stem: Which cost is external to Azure DNS zone hosting?

options.A: Domain registration or renewal charges

optionExplanations.A: The registrar bills domain ownership separately.
optionExplanations.B: These belong to the DNS service.
optionExplanations.C: Queries are a service cost driver.
optionExplanations.D: Tags are metadata, not registrar fees.

questions.learningObjective: Low cost is not no cost
questions.stem: Why should enabled public DNS still be included in a lab budget?

options.A: Every zone creates a Windows VM
options.B: Hosted zones and queries can incur charges
options.D: The lab buys a new domain automatically

optionExplanations.A: The lesson creates no VM.
optionExplanations.B: Low relative cost does not mean free.
optionExplanations.C: Bastion is unrelated here.
optionExplanations.D: It does not manage registration.

questions.stem: Which action inspects the managed zone without changing delegation?

options.A: List DNS zones in the lesson resource group

optionExplanations.A: Azure inspection does not mutate registrar settings.
optionExplanations.B: That changes public DNS authority.
optionExplanations.C: That mutates Azure resources.
optionExplanations.D: Deletion changes hosted content.

questions.stem: What does terraform apply tfplan apply?

options.A: Any file named README.md
options.D: The reviewed changes in the saved plan

optionExplanations.A: Markdown is not a Terraform plan.
optionExplanations.B: This configuration has no registrar resource.
optionExplanations.C: It is scoped to this configuration/state.
optionExplanations.D: A saved plan carries its planned actions.

questions.stem: Why is example.com inappropriate for enabled learning deployment?

options.A: All .com zones are unsupported
options.B: It would create a private endpoint
options.C: It is a documentation placeholder, not the learner's domain
options.D: It selects a special free Azure tier

optionExplanations.A: Azure DNS supports public .com zones.
optionExplanations.B: A public zone does not create endpoints.
optionExplanations.C: The lesson requires deliberate domain ownership.
optionExplanations.D: The name is not a pricing tier.

questions.stem: What production design reduces accidental DNS cross-environment changes?

options.A: Separate approved zones or subdomains with clear ownership
options.B: One shared administrator account without logs

optionExplanations.A: Each authority has a reviewed boundary.
optionExplanations.B: That weakens accountability.
optionExplanations.C: Delegation needs documented recovery.
optionExplanations.D: State exposure is unnecessary and unsafe.

questions.stem: Who should be able to modify a production zone?

options.A: Every visitor who resolves the domain
options.B: Anyone who knows the zone name
options.D: Authorized identities at the required scope

optionExplanations.A: Resolving records grants no management rights.
optionExplanations.B: A name is not authorization.
optionExplanations.C: Repository access is not Azure RBAC.
optionExplanations.D: Scoped permissions limit accidental changes.

questions.stem: What happens to records inside a Terraform-managed zone when the zone is destroyed?

options.A: They transfer to the registrar automatically
options.C: They are removed with the zone

optionExplanations.A: Terraform provides no such transfer.
optionExplanations.B: Public and private zones are distinct.
optionExplanations.C: The zone owns its hosted records.
optionExplanations.D: Deleted hosting cannot continue serving them.

questions.stem: An organization's domain already uses another DNS provider. What is the safe first step?

options.A: Change delegation immediately to finish the lab
options.B: Coordinate ownership and migration with its DNS administrator

optionExplanations.A: That risks live service disruption.
optionExplanations.B: Avoid conflicting delegation and missing records.
optionExplanations.C: That removes the rollback path.
optionExplanations.D: Ownership is still required.

questions.stem: Which plan evidence demonstrates the default optional path?

options.A: A browser opens the repository
options.B: An NS lookup of an unrelated domain succeeds
options.D: A subscription has a friendly name

optionExplanations.A: That does not inspect Terraform actions.
optionExplanations.B: It says nothing about the lesson plan.
optionExplanations.C: The enabled count remains zero.
optionExplanations.D: Names are not resource-change evidence.

questions.stem: What distinguishes this zone from CLZ-290's Private DNS zone?

options.A: It must be attached to every VNet
options.B: It is hosted for public domain delegation
options.D: It grants all clients Azure RBAC

optionExplanations.A: Public hosting does not require VNet links.
optionExplanations.B: Private zones serve linked network resolution.
optionExplanations.C: That is Storage, not DNS.
optionExplanations.D: DNS resolution does not grant authorization.

questions.stem: After delegation, what is needed for a new www hostname to resolve to an IPv4 address?

options.A: An appropriate A record in the hosted zone
options.B: A Key Vault secret named www

optionExplanations.A: An A record maps the name to IPv4.
optionExplanations.B: Secrets do not provide DNS records.
optionExplanations.C: Region changes do not define hostname records.
optionExplanations.D: Terraform backend location is unrelated.

questions.stem: A hostname resolves, but HTTP fails. What does DNS success prove?

options.A: The web application's TLS and health are correct
options.B: All NSGs allow the application's port
options.D: Name resolution worked, not application availability

optionExplanations.A: Those require separate application tests.
optionExplanations.B: DNS does not test network rules.
optionExplanations.C: A lookup is not cleanup evidence.
optionExplanations.D: DNS does not validate the web service.

questions.stem: A learner owns a domain but does not want any Azure zone yet. Which exercise fits?

options.A: Review an enabled owned-domain plan without applying it
options.B: Run apply automatically after any plan

optionExplanations.A: Planning permits review without deployment.
optionExplanations.B: That creates the zone.
optionExplanations.C: That is an external production change.
optionExplanations.D: That weakens the lesson boundary.

questions.stem: Which command confirms the managed resource group is absent after destroy?

options.A: terraform fmt -check

optionExplanations.A: Formatting does not inspect Azure deletion.
optionExplanations.B: A false result checks Azure absence.
optionExplanations.C: That queries an unrelated public domain.
optionExplanations.D: Reading documentation is not deletion evidence.
